item.title: DrawSplat Update: SketchSpace VR Turns Student Drawings into Virtual Rooms
item.description: SketchSpace VR is now available from the DrawSplat Tools dropdown as a standalone classroom solution. Students can print a one-page cube-room template, draw or label six panels, photograph the finished page, and explore the result as an interactive virtual room in the browser. The tool includes privacy-friendly local image handling, crop preview, trim controls, fullscreen viewing, split-view, phone viewer mode, and a language picker. To help students get started, SketchSpace VR also includes five curriculum starter layouts: life cycle room, plant cell model, algebra walkthrough, country profile, and story setting with evidence. A separate teacher guide provides setup notes, lesson ideas, examples, assessment prompts, sharing guidance, and links to the TCEA Panoform posts that inspired this paper-first virtual reality workflow.

item.title: DrawSplat v3.1.8 Update: More Tools, Cleaner Cards, and a Fresher Self-Host Zip
item.description: DrawSplat v3.1.8 is packed with classroom-friendly polish. SplatImage Studio now has smoother paste handling, proportional arrowheads, better crop controls, shape masks, duplicate layers, layer transparency, text alignment, and a bigger Effects menu with mosaic, cubism, pixelate, blur/sharpen-style cleanup, lighten, and darken options. Quiz & Flashcard Studio gets clearer answer cards, so the answer stands out while extra explanation stays visually quieter. Concept Map Studio also gets friendlier import and editing controls, especially when working from Markdown or generated map content. The self-host zip has been rebuilt with the latest code, docs, legal/compliance pages, tools, and release notes, so schools and organizations can grab one current package and run DrawSplat on their own infrastructure. In short: fewer rough edges, more creative tools, and a nicer path for teachers who want the full DrawSplat experience in one download.

item.title: DrawSplat Hub Update: A Protected Admin Space for Classroom, Campus, and District Instances
item.description: DrawSplat Hub now has a clearer public front door and a protected admin path for managing classroom, campus, and district instances. The Hub splash page stays open so people can see what the model looks like, while the live Instances Admin dashboard sits behind Google OAuth for approved administrators. The approved admin accounts are mguhlin@gmail.com and jeguhlin@gmail.com. From the Instances Admin page, a Hub admin can add an independent classroom teacher or place a teacher under a campus. The starter Apps Script registry can create a teacher folder and config file in Google Drive, then share both with the teacher as editor. That keeps setup practical while respecting Google Drive ownership rules. The self-host bundle still includes only the generic Hub and hubcampus demo, so future real campus data stays out of public downloads.

item.title: ControlAltAchieve 💡 #171
item.description: DrawSplat - Resource link I am constantly blown away by the quality of free resources being created with vibe coding. Recently my friend Miguel Guhlin shared with me his latest creation … DrawSplat. He wanted to create an interactive tool for student creativity, drawing some inspiration from programs such as Jamboard, KidPix, and others. His creation, DrawSplat, is a completely free interactive whiteboard tool for K-16 educators and students. It runs in your browser and includes a dizzying array of features including pens, paint, shapes, lines, text, notes, images, diagrams, backgrounds, stickers, graphs, widgets, and so much more. And Miguel seems to add new features everytime I check the site. Head on over to https://drawsplat.org/ to learn more and try it yourself.
